song.title: Les Rita Mitsouko _ Simplified bass line with tabs

guitar.notes: This is a song title (Les Rita Mitsoukos), not an artist; sample_titles indicate the actual artist is Les Rita Mitsouko. Insufficient reliable attribution to assign specific gear.

tone.summary: A foundational, articulate, and slightly overdriven tone simulating a classic upright or electric bass through a clean British stack, emphasizing clarity and deep lows.
corrections: cannot build guitar preset for bass line
requires bass rig not guitar rig

rig.name: Marcia Baila - Les Rita Mitsouko _ Simplified bass line with tabs - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up any low-end hum or rumble from the source material.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for clean signal chains.

blocks.purpose: Provide gentle harmonic saturation and punch to simulate the attack of a plucked bass string.
blocks.gap: The ideal module would be a dedicated Bass Overdrive. Using 'Boost' provides necessary compression and slight grit without losing fundamental low frequencies.

blocks.purpose: Bypass. We need maximum clarity and definition for a bass line, avoiding heavy distortion.
Model a clean, articulate American-style amplifier suitable for simulating the punch of a P-Bass/J-Bass.
blocks.gap: The ideal choice would be a dedicated Bass Amp model. US Deluxe is selected for its clean headroom and defined low end.

alternatives.model: Silver Twin (if more vintage chime is desired)

blocks.purpose: Provide a focused and clear cabinet response that emphasizes the fundamental frequencies of the bass line.
blocks.gap: While 4x12 cabinets are common for guitar, the US 2x12 is chosen here to maintain clarity and focus on the lower mids/bass region without excessive bloom.

alternatives.model: UK Vintage 4x12 (if more girth is needed)

blocks.purpose: Slightly boost the fundamental low frequencies and high-end definition to make the bass line pop in a mix.
blocks.gap: A dedicated Bass EQ would be optimal, but Guitar EQ 2 offers sufficient parametric control for this task.

blocks.purpose: Bypass. The bass line requires consistent tone and articulation, not sweeping filter effects.
Add subtle width and thickness to the tone without muddying the fundamental bass frequencies.
blocks.gap: Chorus is generally used for rhythm guitar, but a very low mix rate can add desirable harmonic richness to simulate thicker strings or pickups.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle depth and space to the performance without distracting from the core rhythm.
blocks.gap: A dedicated Bass Delay would be better, but Digital Delay provides necessary control for a tasteful echo effect.

blocks.purpose: Place the simulated bass line in a natural acoustic space to give it depth and realism.
blocks.gap: Room reverb is versatile, but a Plate or Spring might be more appropriate for punchy bass tones. Room was chosen for its general warmth.

improvements.summary: Upgrade cabinet/IR to better simulate bass frequencies and increase low-end punch.

proposals.reason: US 2x12 is too bright and lacks deep bass girth.
